transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-22
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Holt (Redwood CSM), Samir Patel (Aurora CTO), Emily Chen (Head of ML), Diego Ramos (SWE), Natalie Wong (Data Scientist)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery on embeddings and reranking pipeline architecture, vector DB options, dimensionality, batching/throughput, and private/hosted deployment tradeoffs. Agreed next steps include benchmark run and sharing security docs.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you fitting us in. Today we wanted to understand your current retrieval pipeline and goals for reranking and embeddings.
[00:18] Samir (Aurora CTO): Yeah thanks Jordan. We are re-evaluating our semantic search stack, currently on Elastic + some hand-tuned tfidf, and have been proofing a dense pipeline using Milvus for vectors. There's a lot of noise in short queries and we need reranking to improve precision for top-k.
[00:36] Priya (Redwood SE): Got it. Can you unpack the workload a bit — typical qps, latency SLOs, avg doc length, and embedding dim you're using?
[00:50] Emily (Aurora Head ML): For prod we hit 120 qps peak, tail 95th latency goal is sub-200ms for top-5 retrieval + rerank. Docs are short paragraphs, avg 120–250 tokens. We were prototyping with 768-d embeddings but also testing 1,024 and 1,536 dims.
[01:15] Jordan: Thanks. Quick note on our side: Redwood supports Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC/on-prem deployments. For embeddings and reranking people typically start Hosted for dev and then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput or Private if they need VPC/KMS for compliance.
[01:34] Diego (Aurora SWE): If we go Dedicated, how do we integrate with our vector DB? We currently prefer Milvus but evaluating Redis Vector and Pinecone as well.
[01:45] Priya: Integration is straightforward — you can either store embeddings in your vector DB and call Redwood embeddings API to compute vectors, or you can use our streaming embeddings where Redwood pushes vectors to your endpoint. For reranking we have two patterns: 1) retrieval-then-rerank (score candidates from DB then cross-enc with a small transformer), or 2) index-time cross-encoder pre-scores for hot docs.
[02:12] Natalie (Aurora Data Scientist): Pre-scoring sounds expensive for large corpuses though — do you have recommendations for hybrid search?
[02:22] Priya: Yes, hybrid search combining sparse signals (BM25) + dense embeddings is common. Our recommend is do a coarse retrieval with sparse+ANN then rerank top 50 with a cross-encoder. That keeps latency reasonable while improving top-k quality.
[02:40] Emily: What's your reranker model footprint? We are concerned about latency since cross-encoders are heavy.
[02:47] Priya: Typical cross-encoder for rerank is heavier — if you want sub-200ms for rerank+retrieval you need either an optimized dedicated GPU with batching and KV-cache management, or you rely on lighter bi-encoder scoring with a learned MLP reranker. With Redwood Dedicated you get predictable GPU pools and autoscaling, which helps with consistent latencies.
[03:10] Samir: Is there an option to do the embedding compute in-hosted but rerank on-prem? We need patient data to stay in our VPC for HIPAA reasons.
[03:20] Jordan: Yes, that's a common hybrid deployment — you can call Redwood Hosted embeddings and push vectors into your own Milvus in your VPC, or keep emb compute on-prem with Redwood Private. Also we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments so encryption keys never leave your environment.
[03:38] Diego: When you say batching, what are the token batching vs request batching tradeoffs for rerank? Sometimes we have bursts of small queries.
[03:47] Priya: For rerank, request-level batching across concurrent queries is the biggest win, especially for cross-encoders. Our runtime does continuous batching where it accumulates requests for a short window (10–50ms) to build GPU-efficient batches. There's a latency tail tradeoff but throughput gets much better. For small bursts we can configure max batch delay to meet your SLO.
[04:12] Marcus (Redwood CSM): We also expose per-route controls in the Console so you can set batch windows per endpoint.
[04:20] Natalie: How about embedding dimensionality — we saw 768 vs 1,536 — what's the practical cost / recall difference?
[04:28] Priya: Higher dims often improve recall for semantic nuance, but increase storage and ANN index memory and CPU. For many use cases 768 is a sweet spot; 1,024–1,536 can help on longer context or multi-lingual. We usually recommend running a small ablation on your dataset — Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and target dims.
[04:50] Emily: Do you support quantized embeddings or is that something we do in our DB?
[04:55] Priya: We support producing float16 or int8-friendly representations and we can recommend quantization profiles. Many vector DBs support quantized indexes, but we can help tune it as part of the benchmark.
[05:07] Samir: For throughput, can Redwood Dedicated sustain sustained 120 qps reranking at top-5 with cross-encoder?
[05:17] Priya: It depends on cross-encoder size and batch config. With a medium cross-encoder (eg 6–8M params reranker) and optimized kernels on A10/A100 class GPUs we can hit those numbers with 1–2 GPUs per 100 qps depending on batching. We'll validate in a benchmark.
[05:36] Jordan: We also do smart routing — if Dedicated saturates we can overflow to hosted or a cheaper variant to keep the app online, configurable via rollout policies.
[05:48] Diego: What about vector DB connectors — are there native connectors for Milvus, Pinecone, Redis?
[05:55] Priya: We have reference connectors and ingestion examples for Milvus, Pinecone, Redis-Vector, and pgvector. For most customers it's just a small sync job. We'll share the code repo link.
[06:05] Natalie: Any gotchas with hybrid search latency? Sometimes network hops to DB in another AZ add 30–50ms.
[06:13] Priya: Yes, network hops matter. Co-locating your vector DB and Redwood Dedicated in the same region/availability zone is recommended. For Private or VPC, you can minimize cross-AZ traffic. Also enabling local caching (prefix/KV cache) can reduce hot-doc fetch latency.
[06:32] Emily: On the security side, we need SOC 2 and audit logs, permissioning per route, and SSO integration. How do you handle RBAC and logs?
[06:41] Jordan: Redwood supports RBAC, SAML/SSO integrations, and detailed audit logs at token and request level. We can provide SOC 2 report and architecture diagrams; for Private we support MCP and bring-your-own KMS so keys are customer-managed.
[06:56] Samir: What about data retention for embeddings? Are those stored in Redwood if we use hosted embedding compute?
[07:03] Priya: By default Hosted does retain transient logs for troubleshooting but we can enable policies to not persist vectors and we have options for short retention or delete-on-ingest for compliance. For Dedicated and Private, you have control over storage behavior.
[07:18] Jordan: Ok quick qualification: timeline — when are you looking to start a pilot? Budget? Stakeholders?
[07:25] Samir: We want a pilot in the next 2–3 weeks, budget TBD but stakeholder group includes product, infra, and legal. Acceptance criteria will be top-5 MRR uplift and <=200ms 95th rerank latency.
[07:40] Priya: Great, we'll propose a 2-week benchmark: Redwood runs both hosted and Dedicated runs against your dataset slice, we measure recall@5, latency p95, and cost per 1M queries. We'll include quantization and dim variations.
[07:56] Diego: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[07:59] Priya: A 5–10k document slice, representative queries (50–200), and a clear metric rubric. Also note any blocked content; if HIPAA applies mark PII.
[08:14] Emily: We'll get that over. Also please include comparisons vs Pinecone and an estimate for moving to Redis Vector if needed.
[08:23] Jordan: We have a TCO sheet that compares Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for different qps and dedupe in the cost assumptions; I'll send that.
[08:32] Samir: One more thing — we're interested in hybrid reranking where a lightweight bi-encoder filters and a cross-encoder reranks top-10. Is that pattern supported natively?
[08:44] Priya: Yes that's common. We can implement a two-stage pipeline in Redwood with per-route invocation and piping outputs. You can do the bi-encoder in the DB/edge and call Redwood for the cross-encoder rerank, or host both on Redwood Dedicated.
[08:59] Natalie: Do you have reference latency numbers for that two-stage approach?
[09:03] Priya: Typical numbers: bi-encoder retrieval p95 ~30–60ms (ANN query), cross-encoder rerank on a dedicated GPU with batching for top-10 is ~60–120ms depending on model size and batch window. So combined often sits around 100–180ms p95 with good infra.
[09:23] Marcus: We'll capture those as part of the benchmark and instrument the token and request-level breakdown in Console.
[09:29] Samir: Any compliance or legal gotchas we should be aware of if we choose Hosted for emb compute?
[09:36] Jordan: For PHI/PII you should avoid sending raw data to Hosted unless you have contractual protections; many customers keep emb compute on-prem or in Private when HIPAA is in play. We can work through a Data Processing Addendum and BAA if needed.
[09:51] Emily: Ok makes sense. Can you also share your SOC 2 report and architecture?
[09:55] Jordan: Yes, I'll attach the security packet after the call.
[09:59] Diego: One last question — do you support hybrid search scoring that combines sparse and dense scores at query time? How is normalization handled?
[10:07] Priya: We do. Our Retrieval service supports score fusion strategies (linear comb, rank fusion). We also help tune normalization so BM25 and cosine are comparable — often using z-score or min-max on training queries.
[10:22] Samir: Great, so immediate next steps: we will share data slice and queries, Redwood to run benchmark and send pricing/security docs.
[10:29] Jordan: Correct. Marcus will coordinate the pilot timeline once we have the dataset.
[10:34] Marcus: I'll follow up with a calendar invite and benchmark plan doc.
[10:39] Emily: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[10:41] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll send the TCO, security docs, and set up the benchmark.

Notes/Links mentioned: Redwood TCO spreadsheet (link sent after call), Security pack (SOC2/BAA), Connectors repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/vector-connectors (reference), Benchmark template doc.

End of transcript.
